exposure: women with faecal symptoms after OASIS
women with normal investigations after OASIS
cohort: 50 women who had obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIS) in a previous pregnancy
finding: Mode of delivery in a subsequent pregnancy after OASIS based on symptoms, anal manometry, and endoanal ultrasound helps in preserving anal sphincter function and avoiding unnecessary caesarean sections.
mod_finding: Worsening of fecal symptoms and reduction in anal pressures were not observed in planned vaginal delivery or elective caesarean section groups.
